articles.title: Rise in poverty is ‘a wake-up call for the world’, UN development chief says

events.summary: Multidimensional poverty expanded for the first time in 15 years, affecting 1.2 billion people globally. UN development officials described the trend as an urgent alarm regarding basic living standards.
events.why: Reversing a 15-year downward trend in extreme poverty undermines long-term global stability, public health, and human capital.

articles.title: Sudan: Drought and war push Darfur and Kordofan towards famine
Conflict, drought increasing risk of famine in Sudan: Monitor

events.summary: The risk of famine is mounting in Sudan's Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan regions due to active conflict compounded by severe El Niño drought. The alert was issued on Monday by the UN-backed global hunger monitor.
events.why: Millions of civilians face life-threatening starvation where war and extreme weather intersect to disable food systems and aid delivery.

articles.title: ‘Efficiency has limits’: UNHCR chief warns refugee protection is buckling under cuts

events.summary: UNHCR has received only $3 billion of its required $8.5 billion budget while serving 117 million forcibly displaced individuals. Leadership warned that the global refugee protection framework is buckling under funding deficits.
events.why: Severe shortfalls in refugee funding force dramatic cuts to basic humanitarian provisions and asylum system operations worldwide.

articles.title: ‘These attacks must cease immediately’: Guterres condemns deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh airport

events.summary: A Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's primary international airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300. UN Secretary-General António Guterres issued an immediate condemnation demanding a halt to such strikes.
events.why: A direct, mass-casualty strike on a sovereign capital's civil aviation hub poses major escalation risks across the Middle East.

articles.title: Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Tusk

events.summary: Polish police detained a man suspected of plotting an assassination against Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Credible intelligence also indicated potential attacks targeting the defense minister.
events.why: Assassination plots targeting head-of-government officials pose severe risks to national and regional political stability.

articles.title: Why the US is bringing back firing squads

events.summary: The planned execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan would mark the US Army's first use of a firing squad since 1945.
events.why: It signifies a historic shift in US military capital punishment practice after an eight-decade hiatus.

articles.title: Mourners killed by Kenya police at ex-PM's national farewell not part of violence, BBC finds

events.summary: A BBC Africa Eye investigation found that mourners killed by Kenyan police at a memorial were far from any scuffles. The finding was based on an analysis of 1,500 videos and images from the event.
events.why: It provides evidence of fatal state violence against peaceful mourners, raising critical human rights and police accountability issues.

articles.title: Children among 139 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says

events.summary: A boat carrying 305 people capsized off the coast of Obock, Djibouti, while traveling toward Yemen. At least 139 people, including children, were killed according to the UN.
events.why: It is a mass-casualty maritime disaster affecting vulnerable migrants on a dangerous cross-regional migration route.

articles.title: Cyberattack on French supermarkets causes fires, millions in losses
Hundreds of supermarkets in France hit by ‘unprecedented’ cyberattack
Hundreds of French supermarkets hit by a cyberattack that  defrosted refrigeration systems
Hackers force French supermarket fridges to heat up to 50C in ‘unprecedented’ cyber-attack

events.summary: A cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigeration systems left shelves empty across France. The incident defrosted storage units, causing fires and millions in commercial losses.
events.why: It demonstrates a novel attack vector targeting physical critical retail infrastructure to directly disrupt food supply chains.

articles.title: General Assembly adopts pandemic declaration, but not by consensus

events.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response with 153 votes in favor. The resolution failed to reach consensus, facing opposition from Argentina, Israel, and the United States, alongside two abstentions.
events.why: Divergence by key global actors hampers coordinated multilateral frameworks necessary to respond to future worldwide health emergencies.

articles.title: Trump faces growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia

events.summary: Lawmakers from both the Republican and Democratic parties have criticized plans to import diesel from Russia. The deal was announced weeks ahead of the US midterm elections.
events.why: Shifts in US-Russia energy trade carry major geopolitical and sanctions-related ramifications.

articles.title: Why Moscow is staying tight-lipped on Trump's energy ceasefire
Trump insists energy ceasefire holds as Ukraine reports new Russian strikes
Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
Trump announced a partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire. Did either country know about it?

events.summary: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky indicated openness to a ceasefire on energy infrastructure, while Moscow has offered little official response despite claims of a deal. Reports of ongoing Russian strikes persist as diplomatic conditions remain uncertain.
events.why: A pause in strikes against critical energy grids could drastically alter civilian winter survival and wartime economic resilience in the region.

articles.title: Djibouti shipwreck: Death toll rises to 139 as 84 remain missing

events.summary: At least 139 migrants died and 84 remain missing after a vessel capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the International Organization for Migration.
events.why: The incident marks a catastrophic loss of life along dangerous maritime migration corridors connecting the Horn of Africa and the Gulf.

articles.title: Poland stabbings driven by online glorification of violence, Tusk says

events.summary: Prime Minister Donald Tusk attributed recent school attacks to the online glorification of violence. The stabbings across Polish schools this week left one person dead and several others injured.
events.why: Fatal school violence has triggered direct political and security interventions at the national level.

articles.title: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears

events.summary: The UN Security Council was informed that Colombia's 2016 peace accord is facing severe strain from rising domestic insecurity. Officials emphasized that the landmark agreement must be preserved to prevent further instability.
events.why: The deterioration of Colombia's peace deal threatens a resurgence of widespread armed conflict and instability across South America.

articles.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s fragile transition – economic strain, Israeli incursions and progress towards elections

events.summary: The UN Security Council convened to address Syria's transition amid persistent economic turmoil, ongoing Israeli incursions in the south, and sectarian strife in Sweida. Concurrently, Damascus reported updates regarding its chemical weapons program and electoral planning.
events.why: Simultaneous internal economic decay, sectarian conflict, and foreign military actions complicate any path toward post-war stability in Syria.

articles.title: UN aid operation underway in Nepal following fresh floods

events.summary: United Nations agencies mobilized emergency relief after flash floods swept through Nepal's central Gorkha district, destroying homes and bridges. The disaster occurred just weeks after catastrophic flooding struck northern areas of the country.
events.why: Repeated flash floods severely damage fragile rural infrastructure and stretch humanitarian relief resources in vulnerable communities.

articles.title: US detains man accused in multi-billion Venezuelan money laundering scheme

events.summary: US authorities detained Álvaro Pulido, who was accused in a multi-billion-dollar Venezuelan money laundering scheme. US officials had previously offered a $10m reward for information leading to his arrest.
events.why: It marks a major enforcement action against international money laundering involving billions of dollars tied to Venezuela.

articles.title: Boardroom feud tests trusted Indian business empire

events.summary: An ongoing boardroom dispute has created uncertainty over leadership succession and corporate governance at a major Indian conglomerate.
events.why: Governance instability at leading national conglomerates can impact broad commercial and financial market confidence.

articles.title: Death threats and isolation - the cost of fighting sexual violence in Iraq

events.summary: Women in Iraq report facing death threats, social pressure, and isolation for speaking out against sexual violence. Many continue to share their experiences publicly despite severe safety concerns.
events.why: It highlights acute safety and human rights threats confronting civil society advocates and survivors in Iraq.

articles.title: Pupil arrested after two teachers shot at French school

events.summary: A 14-year-old student was detained after a shooting at a French middle school. Both the principal and a teacher sustained injuries in the incident.
events.why: It represents a severe breach of school safety and armed violence in an educational institution.
